root_cause.text: The loop in `pipapo_drop()` unconditionally evaluates `rulemap[i + 1].n` on every iteration, including the last where `i == m->field_count - 1`, causing an out-of-bounds read beyond the stack-allocated `rulemap` array.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states that `rulemap` is declared as `rulemap[NFT_PIPAPO_MAX_FIELDS]` (size 16), and KASAN reports a stack-out-of-bounds at offset 164, exactly 4 bytes past the end of the array. The patch replaces `rulemap[i + 1].n` with `0` on the last iteration to avoid the access.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a boolean flag to identify the last field in the pipapo drop loop for future conditional handling.
intent_record.what: Added a boolean variable `last` initialized to true when the current field index equals the last field index (field_count - 1) inside the loop over fields in pipapo_drop.
intent_record.how: This variable is computed each iteration but is not used in the shown code; it is likely intended for use later in the function to conditionally execute code only for the last field.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix out-of-bounds access in pipapo_drop by using the last flag to guard against reading beyond the rulemap array and to pass the correct flag to pipapo_unmap.
intent_record.what: In pipapo_drop, the fifth argument to pipapo_unmap changed from rulemap[i + 1].n to last ? 0 : rulemap[i + 1].n, and the sixth argument changed from i == m->field_count - 1 to last.
intent_record.how: When the last flag indicates the final field, the function no longer accesses rulemap[i + 1].n (which would be out-of-bounds) and instead passes 0. The last argument now directly uses the last variable instead of repeating the field count check.

vuln_statements.explanation: This condition accesses rulemap[i+1].n on every iteration of the loop without checking if i is the last index (i == field_count-1), causing an out-of-bounds read beyond the stack-allocated rulemap array.
